**Responsibilities:**
You will help build — and rewrite — an industrial recommendation system serving a billion-scale user base across short-video, livestream, and product scenarios, covering retrieval, pre-ranking, ranking, and blending end to end. Every iteration ships to production and directly moves user experience and GMV.
  
  

* Scale recommendation models like LLMs. Push ranking models from hundreds of millions to billions of parameters and chart the scaling laws of recommendation: behavior-corpus pretraining; multi-scenario, multi-task, multi-stage joint training; ultra-long behavior-sequence modeling (10K+ events) with KV caching, sequence compression, user/generation (U-G) disaggregated serving, speculative decoding, and dynamic batching — raising MFU while holding a strict millisecond latency budget.
* Build one-stage generative retrieval. Reframe retrieval as generation: tokenize the item space into semantic IDs (RQ-VAE / SID) and train autoregressive models, grounded in MLLM semantics, to generate what a user wants next — collapsing the traditional "multi-channel retrieval + ranking" funnel into a single generative stage. The open problems span the full stack: item tokenizers that balance semantic content against collaborative signal, and SIDs that stay stable while millions of new items arrive daily; post-training the generator directly on live user feedback (preference optimization, GRPO-style RL); and decoding under a millisecond budget — beam search, decoding constrained to the valid item space, and test-time scaling that trades inference compute for better recommendations. The prize is a system freed from its path dependence on ID memorization, where cold-start generalization comes from semantics rather than impression history.
* Inject world knowledge. Use large models' real-world knowledge to mine latent user interests and semantic representations beyond what pure ID co-occurrence can express; use reasoning models to run explicit chain-of-thought inference over long-horizon user intent, making the system materially better at discovery and novelty.
* Push training and inference to the hardware limit. Custom CUDA / Triton fused kernels, memory and computation-graph optimization, distributed training and inference acceleration, mixed precision and low-bit quantization — engineered for what makes recommendation hard: sparse embeddings, variable-length sequences, and many task heads.
* Rewrite R&D with agents. We are embedding coding agents deep into the algorithm-development loop: automated feature mining and pipeline generation, experiment configuration and training orchestration, automated evaluation and online-diagnosis attribution, bad-case mining and patrol. You will be both a user and a builder of this system.
* Do original work on open problems. Long-term value modeling, repurchase and retention, transaction attribution, fatigue modeling, new-user recommendation, incremental value modeling, interest exploration, LLM4Rec — problems where industry has no standard answers. We expect, and support, original research: internal papers, patents, and publication at top external venues.

* Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics or a related discipline.
* Solid ML and engineering fundamentals: you understand the math behind the models, and you write clean, efficient, reproducible code with a strong command of algorithms and data structures.
* Deep research or engineering practice in at least one of: LLMs / foundation models, NLP, CV, RL, or recommendation / search / ads — and you can articulate why you made the choices you made, and where they fell short.
* Genuine enthusiasm for LLM / LRM techniques: you want frontier methods live in production, not parked at offline metrics.
* Strong problem definition and decomposition: faced with an ambiguous problem that has no standard answer, you find your own foothold.

* Scale recommendation models like LLMs. Push ranking models from hundreds of millions to billions of parameters and chart the scaling laws of recommendation: behavior-corpus pretraining; multi-scenario, multi-task, multi-stage joint training; ultra-long behavior-sequence modeling (10K+ events) with KV caching, sequence compression, user/generation (U-G) disaggregated serving, speculative decoding, and dynamic batching — raising MFU while holding a strict millisecond latency budget.
* Build one-stage generative retrieval. Reframe retrieval as generation: tokenize the item space into semantic IDs (RQ-VAE / SID) and train autoregressive models, grounded in MLLM semantics, to generate what a user wants next — collapsing the traditional "multi-channel retrieval + ranking" funnel into a single generative stage. The open problems span the full stack: item tokenizers that balance semantic content against collaborative signal, and SIDs that stay stable while millions of new items arrive daily; post-training the generator directly on live user feedback (preference optimization, GRPO-style RL); and decoding under a millisecond budget — beam search, decoding constrained to the valid item space, and test-time scaling that trades inference compute for better recommendations. **About Skan**
Skan automates automation. We capture how work actually happens across an organization and autonomously turn that observation into automation. We are now building toward agentic automation of that work: systems that operate over observed process data and generate Agentic Operating Procedures, structured and auditable playbooks mined from direct observation that allow agents to understand the steps, decisions, branches, and exceptions that define how work is actually performed.
  
  
We are a small and passionate team of researchers, engineers, and domain experts working on the next generation of agentic automation: self-discovered AI agents that can understand and operate real enterprise software.
  
  
**About The Role**
Before an agent can reliably operate software on a user's behalf, it needs to understand what should happen next and why: the underlying process, its steps, decision points and governing logic, branches, variations, dependencies, and long-tail edge cases. In practice, this knowledge is rarely represented explicitly. It is distributed across messy event logs, unstructured documents, screen recordings, UI interaction traces, historical executions, and the tacit knowledge of domain experts.
  
  
As an Applied Scientist on this team, you will work across teams to develop process-agnostic, scalable learning systems that recover the latent structure, decision logic, and dynamics underlying complex process execution trajectories from sparse, noisy, highly correlated observations spanning substantial behavioral heterogeneity and organizational scale.
  
  
You will take heterogeneous data such as action logs, noisy screen traces, semi-structured documents, and variant-heavy workflows, and build systems that recover canonical process structure, meaningful variations, decision rules, dependencies, exceptions, and provenance. These representations are consumed by downstream agentic execution systems and must preserve enough detail for an agent to act correctly while remaining structured, compact, transparent, and auditable.
  
  
The same observational data and learned representations also contribute directly to our work on computer-use models for last-mile interaction with enterprise software.
  
  
The problems here rarely arrive with clean formulations. You may begin with a branch the system consistently fails to recover, two superficially different execution paths that should collapse into the same process, or an algorithm that works across thousands of traces but fails at millions. Your job is to turn those failures into tractable research problems: identify the right abstraction, formulate hypotheses, design evaluations that isolate the problem, and develop methods that solve it. Depending on the problem, this may draw from process and decision mining, graph algorithms, structured prediction, representation learning, information retrieval, program synthesis, model post-training and distillation, or agentic systems.
  
  
We care less about allegiance to a particular technique than about finding the simplest method that reliably recovers the underlying structure and scales.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Process discovery and representation: Build pipelines that discover, extract, and formalize end-to-end business processes from event logs, UI interaction traces, screen recordings, and unstructured documents.
* Develop algorithms for process variant detection, noise removal, and trace consolidation, turning noisy, high-cardinality action sequences into clean canonical representations.
* Design representations that preserve the information downstream agents need while collapsing irrelevant execution-level variation.
* Study the tradeoff between abstraction and fidelity: determine when superficially different trajectories represent the same underlying behavior and when small differences encode materially different decisions.
* Build retrieval and grounding systems that incorporate SOPs, documents, and domain knowledge when process understanding requires evidence beyond execution traces.
* Evaluation and reliability: Develop rigorous evaluation frameworks for process discovery and extraction, including LLM-as-Judge pipelines, conformance checking against ground-truth processes, and regression suites that catch subtle degradation.
* Develop evaluation methods for settings where there may not be a single canonical ground truth, including behaviorally equivalent process representations.
* Enumerate and systematically test exception paths, conditional branches, loops, rare variants, and the failure modes that naive extraction approaches miss.
* Make deliberate algorithmic tradeoffs so systems remain tractable across millions of traces and thousands of variants, including choices around data structures, approximation, indexing, and level of abstraction.
* Diagnose failures in production and turn recurring failure patterns into new algorithmic or research directions.
* Collaboration: Work closely with the computer-use agents team so the representations you produce are expressed at the right level of abstraction, contain the necessary execution context, and are robust enough for downstream autonomous execution.
* Work across research, engineering, and product to move promising methods from prototype to production and measure their effect on downstream agent behavior.

**Requirements**

* Problem Decomposition and Algorithmic Thinking: You can take a loosely defined problem, such as recovering a reliable process from messy action logs, decompose it into tractable sub-problems, reason carefully about edge cases, and arrive at an approach. You are comfortable reasoning from first principles about data structures, graph algorithms, approximation, indexing, and time and space complexity when algorithms must operate over millions of executions.
* ML, DL Breadth: Strong working knowledge across representation learning, sequence modeling, clustering, structured prediction, information retrieval, generative modeling, and modern foundation-model adaptation. You have the judgment to recognize when a problem calls for a learned model, an algorithmic solution, an LLM-based system, or some combination of the three.

You can identify the core idea inside a method, understand the assumptions that make it work, determine whether those assumptions hold in your setting, and adapt the idea into a working prototype.
* Research Judgment: You can distinguish a difficult engineering problem from a research problem, design experiments that isolate the important variable, and abandon an elegant approach when the evidence suggests a simpler method works better.

You understand the failure modes that arise when model outputs are used to recover structured process knowledge from noisy evidence.
